questions.question: The marked price of an article is 160 percent of the cost price. If 20 percent discount is given, then what will be the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = 160% of Cost Price (CP)

Discount = 20% of MP

Find Profit Percentage

**Concept:**

Profit or Loss is calculated on CP.

**Solution:**

Let the CP = 100 (For simplicity)

Hence, MP = 160 (As MP is 160% of CP)

Discount = 20% of MP = 20% of 160 = 32

Selling Price (SP) = MP - Discount = 160 - 32 = 128

Profit = SP - CP = 128 - 100 = 28

Profit Percentage = (Profit/CP) × 100 = (28/100) × 100 = 28%

**Hence, the profit percentage is 28% (Option 1).**

questions.question: The average age of 15 members of a committee is increased by 4 years when two members whose ages are 60 years and 70 years are replaced by the two new members. What is the average age of the new members?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Average age of 15 members increased by 4 years when two members of ages 60 and 70 are replaced

**Concept: **

Average is the sum of all observations divided by the number of observations.

**Solution:**

Total increase in age = 15 members × 4 years/member = 60 years

Sum of ages of new members = Sum of ages of replaced members + Total increase in age = 60 + 70 + 60 = 190 years

Average age of new members = Sum of ages of new members/Number of new members = 190/2 = 95 years

**Hence, the average age of the new members is 95 years (Option 4).**

questions.question: If A can do a work in 21 days and B can do the same work in 28 days. In how many days will they complete the work if they work on alternate days?
questions.solution:
A's work time = 21 days

B's work time = 28 days

Find time to complete work if A and B work alternately

**Concept: **Work done is inversely proportional to time taken. If they work on alternate days, their work done adds up.

B's work/day = 1/28

**Hence, they will complete the work in 24 days.**

questions.question: What is that greatest four-digit number which when divided by 3 and 4 leaves remainder 2 in each case?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

LCM of divisors (3, 4) = 12.

Largest 4-digit number divisible by 12 is 9996.

Required number = (Largest number divisible by 12) + Remainder.

Required number = 9996 + 2 = 9998.

**∴ The correct answer is 9998.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Divisors = 3 and 4, Remainder in each case = 2.

Formula: Number = [LCM(Divisors) × k] + Remainder.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f537dce4f75253a0ac5a690f64f9b27b23cfa01770d157fe273a5c1fba1ffee7.png] 

⇒ Step 1: Find LCM of 3 and 4.

⇒ LCM(3, 4) = 12.

⇒ Step 2: Divide the greatest 4-digit number (9999) by 12 to find the remainder.

⇒ 9999 ÷ 12 = 833 with a remainder of 3.

⇒ Step 3: Find the greatest 4-digit number exactly divisible by 12.

⇒ 9999 − 3 = 9996.

⇒ Step 4: Add the common remainder 2 to this value.

⇒ 9996 + 2 = 9998.

**∴ The correct answer is 9998.**

**__Additional Information__**

General Form for Same Remainder

Any number that leaves a remainder 'r' when divided by x, y, and z is of the form: [LCM(x, y, z) × k] + r, where k is an integer.

LCM and HCF Relationship

For any two numbers a and b, HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b.

Greatest n-digit Number logic

To find the greatest n-digit number divisible by L, subtract (n-digit max ÷ L)'s remainder from the n-digit max value.</p

questions.question: A person bought an article and sold it at a loss of 10 percent. If he had boughs it for 30 percent less price and sold it for Rs. 90 more, then he would earn a profit of 35 percent. What is the cost price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the initial Cost Price (CP) be 100 units.

Initial Selling Price (SP) at 10% loss = 100 − 10 = 90 units.

New CP at 30% less price = 100 − 30 = 70 units.

New SP at 35% profit on the New CP = 70 + (35% of 70) = 70 + 24.5 = 94.5 units.

Difference in SP = 94.5 − 90 = 4.5 units ⇒ 4.5 units = Rs. 90 ⇒ 1 unit = Rs. 20 ⇒ 100 units = Rs. 2000.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial loss percentage = 10%

New cost price is 30% less than the initial cost price.

New selling price is Rs. 90 more than the initial selling price.

New profit percentage = 35%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7e5f7baf8093748285e5c0be0140eaa4d11082494bfc78234cb5bab83da01561.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the initial Cost Price (CP) be x.

⇒ Initial Selling Price (SP) = x − (10% of x) = 0.9x

⇒ New Cost Price (CP) = x − (30% of x) = 0.7x

⇒ New Selling Price (SP) = 0.7x + (35% of 0.7x)

⇒ New SP = 0.7x × 1.35 = 0.945x

According to the given condition, New SP is Rs. 90 more than the Initial SP:

⇒ 0.945x − 0.9x = 90

⇒ 0.045x = 90

⇒ x = 90 ÷ 0.045

⇒ x = 2000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when SP > CP (Profit = SP − CP). Loss occurs when CP > SP (Loss = CP − SP). Both profit and loss percentages are strictly calculated on the Cost Price (CP).

Successive Discount

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount percentage is computed as (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Marked Price

Discount is always applied directly on the Marked Price (MP) of an article. Selling Price (SP) is obtained as SP = MP − Discount.
</p

questions.question: What is the smallest integer that is divisible by 12, 22 and 32?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The smallest integer divisible by the given numbers is their Least Common Multiple (LCM).

Numbers: 12, 22, 32

Take the largest number 32. To be divisible by 12 (4 × 3), it needs a factor of 3.

To be divisible by 22 (2 × 11), it needs a factor of 11.

LCM = 32 × 3 × 11 = 1056

**∴ The correct answer is 1056.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 12, 22 and 32.

**Formula Used:**

The smallest integer exactly divisible by a set of numbers is their Least Common Multiple (LCM).

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 12 = 2² × 3

⇒ Prime factorization of 22 = 2¹ × 11

⇒ Prime factorization of 32 = 2⁵

⇒ The LCM is the product of the highest power of each prime factor involved.

⇒ LCM = 2⁵ × 3¹ × 11¹

⇒ LCM = 32 × 3 × 11

⇒ LCM = 96 × 11 = 1056

**∴ The correct answer is 1056.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

It is the smallest positive integer that is perfectly divisible by each of the given numbers.

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

It is the largest positive integer that divides each of the given numbers without leaving a remainder.

Product Rule of Two Numbers

For any two numbers a and b: LCM(a, b) × HCF(a, b) = a × b

LCM of Fractions

LCM of fractions = (LCM of Numerators) ÷ (HCF of Denominators)
</p

questions.question: A train moves at a speed of 30 m/s and crosses a bridge of length 650 metres in 50 seconds. What is the length of the train?
questions.solution:
Given:

Train speed = 30 m/s

Bridge length = 650 m

Time to cross = 50 s

**Concept:**

The total distance covered when a train crosses a bridge is the sum of the length of the train and the length of the bridge. This total distance is equal to the speed of the train times the time it takes to cross the bridge.

**Solution:**

Total distance covered = speed × time = 30 × 50 = 1500 m

Length of train = total distance - bridge length = 1500 - 650 = 850 m

**Hence, the length of the train is 850 metres (Option 3).**

questions.question: What is the major function of a cell wall?

options.text: It works as a storage for material
It provides shape and rigidity to the cell
It is responsible for cell division
It helps in synthesis of carbohydrate

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It provides shape and rigidity to the cell**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cell walls **are a feature of almost all** prokaryotic cells**, as well as many **eukaryotic organisms.**
 
• In addition to providing structural support and maintaining the shape of the cell, The cell wall serves as a **protective barrier** against **physical** and** biological threats.**
 
• It also allows the cell to **withstand** the difference in **osmotic pressure** between the **cell's interior and its environment.**
 
• However, it is not primarily involved in functions such as storage of material, cell division, or the synthesis of carbohydrates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** The structure of a typical cell, whether it is a **prokaryotic cell (such as bacteria)** or a **eukaryotic cell (like those found in plants and animals),** includes several key components:

 
• **Cell Membrane (Plasma Membrane):** It controls the movement of substances in and out of the cell.
 
• **Cytoplasm: **This is the jelly-like substance within the cell membrane, which contains all the organelles.
 
• **Nucleus:** In eukaryotic cells, this organelle contains the cell's DNA and controls the cell's growth, metabolism, and reproduction.
 
• **Mitochondria: ** They generate most of the cell's supply of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), used as a source of chemical energy.
 
• **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER):** There are two types: rough ER, which has ribosomes on its surface, and smooth ER, which lacks ribosomes.
 
• **Golgi Apparatus:** This organelle is involved in the modification, sorting, and packaging of proteins for secretion.
 
• **Lysosomes: **They digest excess or worn-out organelles, food particles, and engulfed viruses or bacteria.
 
• **Ribosomes:** They can be found either floating freely in the cytoplasm or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum.
 
• **Vacuoles:** These are storage bubbles found in cells. 
 
• **Cell Wall (only in plant cells, fungi, and some protists and bacteria):** It provides and maintains the shape of these cells and serves as a protective barrier.
 
• **Chloroplasts (only in plant cells and some protists):** They are the site of photosynthesis, where light energy is converted into chemical energy.

questions.question: ______ is used for the separation of components of a mixture containing two miscible liquids that boil without decomposition and have sufficient difference in their boiling points.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Distillation**:
 
• This is a process used to **separate components of a mixture using differences in their boiling points.**
 
• The mixture is heated to a temperature at which** one or more components evaporate, and then the vapor is condensed and collected separately.**
 
• It's commonly used to **purify liquids, such as alcohol or water, or to separate petroleum into various components, from gasoline to tar.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• This is the process of dissolving carbon dioxide in water.
 
• The process usually involves pressure and low temperatures.
 
• When the pressure is reduced, the carbon dioxide is released from the solution as small bubbles,
 
• Which gives the solution a fizzy taste. It is commonly used in the creation of soft drinks.
 
 
 
• **Sublimation:**
 
 
• This is a process in which a substance goes directly from the solid phase to the gas phase, skipping the liquid phase.
 
• Dry ice (solid carbon dioxide) is a common example of a substance that sublimates.
 
• This process can be used to purify certain substances that sublimate, such as iodine or naphthalene (mothballs).
 
 
 
• **Emulsification: **
 
 
• This is the process of mixing two or more immiscible (unblendable) substances.
 
• This is typically accomplished with the help of a third substance called an emulsifier or emulsifying agent
 
• Which is soluble in both of the mixed substances.
 
• Mayonnaise is a common example of an emulsion
 
• Where oil and vinegar (which are normally immiscible) are mixed together using egg yolk as an emulsifier.
